obligations.text: A Class resource ignores Suite and Case path selectors.

obligations.gap: suite_path is defined but no theorem or neighbour applies it to a Suite containing a slash; every exercised Suite is slash-free (seq![9] or empty). The contrast Suite "A/B" selecting package A.B (and a mutated suite_path that keeps the slash being rejected) is missing.

parent.entailment: The parent states its own counting, run-all, report-before-count and FAILED-line rules, graded directly from test_outcome.rs. B4 restates the exit child (alias). No parent obligation is credited by composition.

obligations.text: A test command fails when any test it ran failed; each case error, method error and failed assertion counts as one failure (the error reads "N failure(s)").
obligations.cases: fixture log with a case error, a method error and two failed assertions (4) vs passing log (0)

obligations.text: Every in-scope test resource runs even after an earlier one fails and the command reports one combined failure; sync -test stops at the first failing resource instead.
obligations.cases: failing first resource followed by passing and empty resources, lifecycle vs sync
obligations.observation: which resources are invoked; aggregate status

obligations.text: Failures are counted after the report file is written, so a .json/.xml file exists for a failing run; an unsupported extension such as .csv fails the command after passing tests and writes no file.
obligations.cases: failing run with .json vs passing run with .csv

obligations.text: The red FAILED lines list the same rows that are counted.
obligations.cases: failing slots after the start, with and without an empty slot
obligations.observation: number of printed FAILED lines vs counted failures

obligations.text: The red FAILED lines appear only when no summary format is active.
obligations.cases: failing run with a summary format (-DUnitTest.Format / device JSON) vs without
obligations.observation: presence of FAILED lines on the device
obligations.gap: displayed_lines has no summary-format input, and readers.rs json_device selects summary content but not whether OutputFailures prints. The pair "failing run with JSON summary format active prints no FAILED lines" vs "same run without a format prints them" is unmodeled (Test.cls::ReportTestResults / Test/Manager.cls::OutputFailures).

obligations.text: A CI job learns the result only from the command status and exit code.
-DUnitTest.FailuresAreFatal=0 makes a run with failing tests succeed, and the process exit code stays 0 even with the terminate flag.
obligations.cases: same failing resources with fatal=true (fails) vs fatal=false (succeeds); exit_code for a succeeded command

obligations.text: With FailuresAreFatal=0 the summary still says "Some tests FAILED", no failure is counted and no FAILED lines are printed.
obligations.cases: non-fatal failing run vs fatal failing run
obligations.observation: summary text; FAILED lines; failure count
obligations.gap: No model connects the fatal flag to the reader: get_all_status/displayed_lines are never conditioned on fatal, and no summary text is modeled. Contrast: non-fatal failing run (ReportTestResults skips GetAllTestsStatus/OutputFailures: 0 counted, 0 FAILED lines, summary "Some tests FAILED") vs fatal run (N counted and printed). Native T2/E4 only.

obligations.text: Test results gather in a per-process list; each test resource counts only the results added after it started, then removes them.
obligations.cases: reader start 1 over [passing parent, failing child] vs start 0

obligations.text: A nested test command counts and removes only its own results; the outer run's earlier results stay, and the outer reader then sees only its own slot (it learns of the inner failure only through the inner command status).
obligations.cases: nested reader after a passing parent slot, then the parent reader from 0
obligations.observation: nested status/count, list after nested read, parent status

obligations.text: A reader that started from an empty list removes the whole list; a later test command starts after leftover entries and ignores them.
obligations.cases: start 0 vs start>0; later reader after a failing leftover slot

obligations.text: When failures are not fatal, or when the report step fails first, nothing is removed from the list.
obligations.cases: non-fatal or report-failure resource vs fatal successful report
obligations.gap: get_all_status always consumes; no model represents ReportTestResults returning before GetAllTestsStatus. Contrast: FailuresAreFatal=0 (or .csv report failure) leaves the run's entries in the list vs the fatal path truncating them; then a later reader started after them ignores them.

obligations.text: FAILED lines are printed only for results after the start, and empty entries are skipped.
obligations.cases: display from slot 1 vs 2; empty middle slot

obligations.text: sync -test runs test resources one at a time and stops at the first resource whose tests fail, so later resources do not run in that sync; test runs every resource.
obligations.cases: failing first resource: sync invokes no later resource vs lifecycle invokes all

obligations.text: sync -test runs the changed test classes.
File changes are recorded before tests run, so a test failure does not undo the sync.
A test resource whose phase list lacks test is skipped and reported as verify-only.
